<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion is at m/z 194.0862 with a characteristic M+2 peak (~32 % of M), indicating a single chlorine atom. Subtracting the monoisotopic mass of ^35Cl gives a remaining mass of 159.117 Da, which matches the formula C₁₂H₁₅. Adding the chlorine gives the molecular formula C₁₂H₁₅Cl, corresponding to a DBE of 5 (aromatic ring + one additional ring). A structure that satisfies this is a chlorobenzene bearing a cyclohexyl substituent (aromatic ring = 4 DBE, cyclohexane ring = 1 DBE). The SMILES for this molecule is **Clc1ccc(cc1)C2CCCCC2**.</thought>
<final_answer>Clc1ccc(cc1)C2CCCCC2</final_answer>
